statement: Some people believe that employees are more productive when they work from home. Others think that working in an office with colleagues produces better results.
question: Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
model:
Since the pandemic forced millions of people to set up desks in their kitchens, the debate over where work is best done has become a lasting one. While remote working clearly suits certain tasks, I believe that most organisations achieve the best results when staff spend at least part of the week together in person.

Those who favour home working point, with some justification, to the time and energy it saves. A commuter who no longer spends ninety minutes a day on crowded trains can devote that time to work or rest, and many employees find that they concentrate better away from the constant interruptions of an open-plan office. Tasks that demand sustained focus, such as writing reports, analysing data or programming, often benefit from this quiet. Several surveys conducted since 2020 have found that a majority of remote workers believe they accomplish more at home.

On the other hand, advocates of the office argue that productivity is not simply a matter of individual output. Much valuable work emerges from informal conversations: a chance remark by the coffee machine can solve a problem that a week of emails had failed to resolve. Junior employees in particular learn by observing experienced colleagues, absorbing how to handle a difficult client or run a meeting, and this kind of tacit knowledge is extremely hard to pass on through a video call. Furthermore, isolation can erode motivation and loyalty over time.

In my view, the most sensible arrangement is a hybrid one, in which days in the office are reserved for collaboration, training and planning, while focused individual work is carried out at home. This combines the efficiency of remote work with the creativity and sense of belonging that a shared workplace fosters.

In conclusion, both positions have merit, but neither extreme serves employers or employees well. A thoughtful balance between the two is likely to produce the strongest results.
